name: NeuralPath FaceAnchor Plus Name-Face Recall
body_location: cranial — compact node at the fusiform gyrus interface, paired with retinal micro-emitter for soft overlay delivery
description:
The FaceAnchor Plus is a memory-assistance implant targeting the specific cognitive bottleneck of face-name association — one of the most commonly reported social memory failures across the human population. A compact processing node interfaces with the fusiform face area of the temporal lobe, intercepting and augmenting the brain's own face-recognition pathway. When the user encounters a face they have previously logged, the system retrieves the associated name, relationship context, last encounter date, and any personal notes the user has added, delivering this information as a soft retinal overlay — a faint, unobtrusive text impression visible only to the user in the lower peripheral field. The retinal micro-emitter that delivers this overlay is a single-point implant at the edge of the sclera, nearly invisible. The system builds its contact database from opt-in social mesh networks, business card exchanges, and manual entry; it does not access public surveillance or unsanctioned identity databases. A privacy handshake protocol ensures that two FaceAnchor users meeting for the first time can mutually share profile data with a single opt-in confirmation.

The FaceAnchor Plus solves a problem that has caused social embarrassment, professional awkwardness, and genuine distress for as long as humans have lived in large anonymous societies. In Meridian 88's dense megacity environment — where a person might interact with dozens of semi-familiar faces in a single day — the implant has become a quiet staple of professional and social life. Event workers, hospitality staff, politicians, and anyone whose job involves managing large networks of relationships were early adopters. But ordinary people who simply hate the moment of not remembering a neighbor's name, a coworker's partner, or a friend-of-a-friend from six months ago have made it one of NeuralPath's best-selling products. For people with prosopagnosia or memory-affecting conditions, it is functionally life-changing.
installation_requirements: Outpatient specialist clinic for fusiform node; retinal emitter can be placed at a licensed pharmacy kiosk; combined procedure takes approximately 60 minutes
maintenance: Contact database syncs automatically via mesh; system firmware updated quarterly; retinal emitter assessed annually for placement drift

side_effects: Mild visual adjustment period of 3–7 days as the user acclimates to peripheral overlay data
Occasional retrieval lag in low-connectivity environments where cloud sync is interrupted, resulting in brief 'blank' moments on familiar faces
Some users report a subtle uncanny sensation during early use — knowing a name before consciously recognizing a face feels briefly disorienting
Rare cases of mild photosensitivity in the retinal emitter eye during the first week
cultural_context: The FaceAnchor Plus has quietly reshaped the social grammar of Meridian 88 in ways that are hard to articulate but widely felt. Forgetting someone's name has become a choice, or at worst a system failure, rather than an inevitable human lapse — and this has shifted social expectations in ways that some find liberating and others find subtly pressuring. In professional contexts, not having some form of name-recall assistance is increasingly unusual; a hiring manager who forgets a candidate's name mid-interview is assumed to be either rude or very old. The implant has also spawned a small etiquette industry around what information it is appropriate to store and display — noting someone's divorce, for example, in your personal notes field, and then letting that note inform how you greet them, raises questions about social surveillance that are still being worked out culturally. Among Tier 1 users, the base model FaceAnchor (the non-Plus predecessor) is common enough to be essentially invisible as a class marker.
known_users: Professionals who manage large relationship networks — event coordinators, sales staff, politicians, executives
People with prosopagnosia, traumatic brain injury affecting memory, or early-stage neurodegenerative conditions
Hospitality workers and customer service staff
Anyone who attends frequent large social events and finds name-recall stressful
Older adults managing age-related memory changes
story_hooks: A FaceAnchor Plus unit begins auto-tagging a face that doesn't exist in the user's contact history — and the overlay information it displays describes a person who, according to city records, died four years ago.

Someone has been systematically corrupting FaceAnchor contact databases across a specific district, swapping names and relationship contexts to cause social chaos — mistaken identities, broken trust, a neighborhood's social fabric quietly unraveling.

A witness to a crime has a FaceAnchor log timestamped to the night in question — but the defense is arguing that FaceAnchor data constitutes an illegal identity database and is inadmissible, and the players are pulled into a legal and ethical battle over what the implant actually records.
